strengthens.note: Order, Disorder, Resonance and the Universe.md
strengthens.claim: Every system has latent structure built into its geometry and physics; chaos constantly probes all possible configurations; when a match occurs, energy stops scattering and accumulates in a coherent pattern.
strengthens.explanation: Directly backs the subject’s claim that latent structure fully determines resonant outcomes and that environmental coupling amplifies the right structure.

strengthens.claim: Resonance is not taste. It is recognition. The things that speak to you only interest you because something similar already existed within you.
strengthens.explanation: Shows internal latent structure matching external patterns, supporting the subject’s view that internal structure determines resonant outcomes.

strengthens.note: Math, Latent Structure, and Why Plato Didn't Need a Soul Realm.md
strengthens.claim: Mathematics discovers latent structure already encoded in reality, showing an immutable underlying structure governs phenomena across domains.
strengthens.explanation: Supports the subject’s claim that latent structure fully determines resonant outcomes.

weakens.claim: A perfect clone with identical arrangement would be a different subject because I am the one looking at the clone; same arrangement does not guarantee same subject.
weakens.explanation: Challenges the subject’s claim that identical latent structure alone determines resonant outcomes, emphasizing subjective continuity beyond mere arrangement.

weakens.note: Order, Disorder, Resonance and the Universe.md
weakens.claim: The universe is bent toward intricate illegible structure and sacrifices local order; resonance can be transient or non‑beneficial.
weakens.explanation: Counters the subject’s hidden assumption that synchronization is inherently stable and beneficial across all scales.

weakens.note: Math, Latent Structure, and Why Plato Didn't Need a Soul Realm.md
weakens.claim: Large regions of pure mathematics have no known physical application, indicating latent structure can exist without manifesting as resonance.
weakens.explanation: Undermines the claim that latent structure alone determines resonant outcomes in every context.

shared_assumptions.note: Order, Disorder, Resonance and the Universe.md
shared_assumptions.assumption: Systems possess an underlying latent structure that governs behavior and resonance occurs when chaos matches that structure.
shared_assumptions.explanation: Both notes treat latent structure as the fundamental driver of resonant phenomena.

shared_assumptions.assumption: Identity (self or resonant outcome) can be traced to an underlying arrangement that persists through time, even as the arrangement changes.
shared_assumptions.explanation: Both view identity as anchored in a persistent arrangement.

shared_assumptions.note: Math, Latent Structure, and Why Plato Didn't Need a Soul Realm.md
shared_assumptions.assumption: Latent structure exists independently of human observation and determines real phenomena.
shared_assumptions.explanation: Both treat latent structure as an objective feature of reality.

tensions.claim: Latent structure is immutable, but the self is a continuously transforming arrangement, suggesting latent structure can change over time.
tensions.explanation: Disagreement on whether underlying structure stays fixed.

tensions.note: Order, Disorder, Resonance and the Universe.md
tensions.claim: Synchronization is inherently stable and beneficial across scales (subject) vs universe sacrifices local order for global complexity, making resonance possibly transient.
tensions.explanation: Contrast between assumed universal benefit and context‑dependent instability.

tensions.note: Math, Latent Structure, and Why Plato Didn't Need a Soul Realm.md
tensions.claim: Scaling analogy treats pendulum clocks, atomic shells, and neural firing as directly transferable, while pure mathematics shows latent structure can exist without resonance.
tensions.explanation: The analogy may overreach; not all latent structures manifest as resonance.
